family: two-representation block list (1^n blocks <-> (10)^k blocks) with an inner bouncer
summary: Keeps a list of blocks in two spellings, solid 1^n and sparse (10)^k with k = floor(n/2)+1, flipping between them on each pass, while an inner bouncer (a 00 marker moving through the 10-runs) reshuffles the block lengths; open.
title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC0LD_1RA0LD_1LA1LB_0RC1RF_1RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC0LD_1RA0LD_1LA1LB_0RC1RF_1RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks that the machine rewrites between a solid spelling (blocks of 1s) and a sparse one (runs of 10); the flip is understood, the reshuffling of the lengths in between is not.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 81,707 cells have been visited and 42,934 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.477). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (110)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (011)^n R; L (011)^n B> 0 R reaches L B> 0 (101)^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (110)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (011)^n R; L (011)^n B> 0 R reaches L B> 0 (101)^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (110)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (011)^n R; L (011)^n B> 0 R reaches L B> 0 (101)^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when state F reads a 1; whether the reshuffled lists ever produce that is the open question.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine stores a list of numbers on its tape and keeps switching between two ways of writing it: as solid blocks of 1s, and as runs of 10 about half as many. In between, a smaller bouncer travels through the list and changes the numbers.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
Each leftward pass halves every block: k = ⌊n/2⌋ + 1.
Two shift rules proved for every length.

sections.heading: One list, two spellings
html: When the head reaches the right end, the tape is a list of solid blocks, each followed by one 0:
On the way back to the left end the head rewrites every block 1^n 0 as (10)^k 1, with k = ⌊n/2⌋ + 1, so the same list is now spelled with runs of 10:

That holds at all 12 such pairs of records in the first 3·107 steps (for every block but the last, still being written). What happens next is a bouncer inside the bouncer: the head returns to the left end again and again while a marker 00 walks right through the runs of 10, a few cells further each time; when it is done the list is spelled solid again, with new lengths. How the marker changes the lengths is the part not worked out yet.
The left end of the tape grows like the square root of the steps; the right end barely moves (cell 25 after 105 steps, cell 36 after 3·106).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.477). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 81,707 cells (60,742 left of the start, 52 right), with a density of 1s of 0.525.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.
